tips.text: Open a trade with Spell Flux, then follow with Rune Prison so the enemy is rooted instead of slowed.
Cast Spell Flux or Rune Prison before Overload; each cast resets Overload's cooldown and charges a rune.
Use Spell Flux on a minion near the enemy so it spreads Flux to them, then hit Overload to bounce to every Flux target.
Charge two runes before Overload when you want to chase or escape, since it then gives you bonus Move Speed.
Aim Overload carefully; the first enemy it hits takes the blast, so a minion in the way can absorb it.
Spam Spell Flux when you can; its short cooldown keeps Flux up for your other spells.
Start Realm Warp before a roam and keep casting while it charges; stun or silence on you will cancel it, so open it somewhere safe.
Watch your mana early; Ryze's spells cost a lot, so don't spam them without a trade or kill in mind.
Stay behind minions when Ahri is in range. Charm stops at the first unit it hits, so a minion in front of you soaks it.
Open with Spell Flux, then use Rune Prison so she is rooted instead of slowed. Follow with Overload for the bonus damage.
Trade hard while Spirit Rush is on cooldown. Ahri is much easier to kill and harder to escape with then.
Use Rune Prison's slow or root to stop her walking onto you after a missed Charm. Then step out of her range.
Keep Rune Prison for when Akali dashes in; with Flux on her it roots her instead of slowing, so she can't get away.
Put Flux on Akali with Spell Flux early and often; it has a short cooldown, and Overload then hits much harder.
Fight her when she is low on Energy; Five Point Strike costs a lot, so she has little to trade back with.
When Akali vanishes in Twilight Shroud, stop chasing. Step away from the smoke and wait for her to come out.
Return to base when your Health gets low and Akali has Perfect Execution ready.
Start trades with Spell Flux, then use Rune Prison on the marked Akshan so he is rooted instead of slowed.
Finish your combo with Overload on a Fluxed Akshan; it hits harder and bounces to nearby Fluxed enemies.
Cast Rune Prison and Spell Flux first so Overload comes back fast. Overload keeps going past the first enemy hit, so line it up with minions in the way.
Hold Rune Prison for when Akshan swings with Heroic Swing; a root punishes his dive.
Stay out of Avengerang's line when you can; it returns and can hit you twice.
Stay out of a straight line with Anivia and sidestep Flash Frost; the stun only lands if you are caught near where the ice ends.
Start trades with Spell Flux, then use Rune Prison so she is rooted instead of slowed and cannot slip away.
Follow Rune Prison and Spell Flux with Overload to hit her hard. Each cast also lets you fire Overload again sooner.
Fight her while she is still low level and short on mana. Glacial Storm drains her mana quickly and needs her to stay inside it.
When her egg appears, do not stop to chase it unless it is safe. Rebirth leaves her helpless for a few seconds, so use that time to push or take a camp.
Do not walk into her Glacial Storm once it is fully formed. It slows you and hurts a lot, so stay out of the area.
Watch for Annie's Pyromania counter under her health bar. When it is full, stay out of her Disintegrate and Incinerate range.
Open with Spell Flux, then use Rune Prison to root her. Follow with Overload for extra damage.
Her Disintegrate has a long range and refunds mana on a kill, so do not let your minions drop low in front of her.
Do not cast Realm Warp where Annie can stun you. Being stunned while it charges cancels the portal.
Cast Spell Flux first, then Rune Prison, so the enemy is rooted instead of slowed and can't fly away.
Fire Overload at a Flux-marked Aurelion Sol for its big bonus damage, then use the Move Speed it gives to step out of his range.
Stun him or root him while he channels Breath of Light; a long beam gets stronger the longer he stays on you.
Walk out of Singularity's edge early. Standing in the center for long can get you executed at low health.
Watch for Falling Star's delay and walk sideways out of it. It stuns, so don't stay clumped with allies.
Cast Spell Flux first, then Rune Prison, so Aurora is rooted instead of slowed and can't hop away.
Rune Prison needs a target, so aim it at Aurora just as she lands from Across the Veil.
Aurora's Twofold Hex is a straight line, so sidestep it. Don't stand still trading with her.
Use Spell Flux on her often to keep Flux up, since it has a short cooldown. Then Overload hits much harder.
Stay out of her Between Worlds ring unless you must fight there. Leaving it slows you.
Start trades with Spell Flux, then follow with Rune Prison so Azir is rooted instead of slowed and can't step away from your next blast.
Fire Overload after Spell Flux or Rune Prison; it hits harder on Flux targets and spreads to nearby enemies that have Flux.
Hit Azir when his soldiers are far from him or have expired. Without them he has little damage to hit back with.
Rune Prison and Spell Flux are targeted, so Azir can't dodge them. Use them freely to poke him, and keep Overload for when it can hit.
Stay out of the line between Azir's soldiers and you. Stand away from them, because their stabs reach you from range.
If Azir's Shifting Sands dash lands on you, don't chase him. Fight back after the shield ends.
Stay out of Sear's line, especially behind minions; it ends at the first unit hit, so keep a minion between you and Brand.
Sidestep Pillar of Flame as soon as you see the ground mark; it lands after a short delay.
Open with Spell Flux, then use Rune Prison so the enemy is rooted and cannot dodge your Overload.
Trade right after Brand misses Sear. His cooldown is long, so you can walk up and fight.
When Brand ults, step away from your minions and allies so the fireball has fewer targets to bounce between.
Hit Briar with Rune Prison after Spell Flux so she is rooted, not just slowed. Then she can't run you down.
Keep Rune Prison ready for when Briar leaps in with Head Rush or Blood Frenzy. Root her to cut the fight short.
Trade with Overload while she is far away, and use Spell Flux first to make it hit harder. Briar has to dive to answer you.
Stay away from walls when Briar charges Chilling Scream. A full charge knocks you back, and a wall hit stuns you.
When Briar lands Certain Death, fight back with all your spells. Her prey mark follows her target, so know whether it is you.
Cast Spell Flux first, then Rune Prison, so Cassiopeia is rooted instead of slowed. Finish with Overload for the extra damage on a marked target.
Walk out of Noxious Blast's circle before it lands; it explodes after a short delay and you can sidestep it.
Stay out of Miasma. It slows you and stops your dashes, so you can't escape her follow-up.
Face away from Cassiopeia when she casts Petrifying Gaze, or move out of the cone. You get slowed instead of stunned.
Use Realm Warp to join fights elsewhere or to escape. You can keep casting while it charges, but crowd control cancels it.
Put Rune Prison on Diana after Spell Flux so she is rooted instead of slowed; she can't dash in with Lunar Rush while held.
Sidestep Crescent Strike; once Diana is marked by Moonlight her Lunar Rush comes back quickly, so back away from the marked target.
Keep Spell Flux going on Diana and the minions near her; Overload then hits harder and bounces to everything marked.
Hold your spells when Pale Cascade is up and trade after the orbs and shield are gone.
Stay at long range and poke with Overload; Diana must close the gap to fight you.
Stun or root Diana as she starts Moonfall at level 6; it pulls you in, so keep your distance and save your root for after she lands.
Cast Spell Flux first, then Rune Prison, so Ekko is rooted instead of slowed and can't slip away.
Fire Overload at Ekko once Spell Flux is on him; it hits harder and bounces to other Flux targets, such as his minions.
Use Rune Prison on Ekko when he dashes in with Phase Dive, so he can't easily run off after his hit.
Step out of Parallel Convergence's zone. Ekko has to enter it to stun, so stay clear of it and don't walk into him.
Trade hard while Chronobreak is on cooldown; Ekko can't rewind to undo the damage.
Cast Spell Flux first, then Rune Prison, so Ezreal is rooted instead of slowed and can't kite away.
Use Overload on Ezreal while he has Flux on him; it hits much harder and also spreads to other Flux targets.
Stand behind minions when you trade, so Ezreal's Mystic Shot is stopped before it reaches you.
Spell Flux has a short cooldown, so use it often to keep Flux on Ezreal and to poke him.
Hold Rune Prison until Ezreal uses Arcane Shift, then root him and punish him.
Use Spell Flux first, then Rune Prison, so Fizz is rooted instead of slowed and can't easily slip away.
Hold Rune Prison for when Fizz is out of his dashes. While Playful is on cooldown he has little way to escape the root.
Fizz can't be targeted while he is on his trident, so don't waste Rune Prison or Spell Flux on him then. Wait until he lands.
Poke with Overload from long range while Fizz walks through minions. Keep the distance so Urchin Strike has to cost him a dash.
Stay away from minions when Fizz's trident glows. His empowered attack and bonus damage hurt a lot, so don't trade in melee.
Watch for Chum the Waters. If the fish sticks to you, move away from where it hits; stay out of the shark's area.
Start with Spell Flux, then Rune Prison, so Galio is rooted rather than just slowed.
Do not cast into a charging Galio; Shield of Durand shrinks your damage, so wait for the shield to end.
Stay out of Justice Punch range and move sideways; it stops at the first champion and cannot cross walls.
Aim Overload at Fluxed enemies for bonus damage; keep your distance so Galio cannot easily reach you.
Walk up and hit Hwei with Spell Flux, then follow with Rune Prison to root him instead of slowing him. That sets up your damage.
Cast Overload on a Flux target for extra damage; casting Spell Flux or Rune Prison first makes your next Overload faster and more powerful.
Rush Hwei right after he casts a Torment spell like Crushing Maw. He is vulnerable then, and your short cooldowns let you trade hard.
Keep moving sideways in lane. Severing Bolt is slow, and it hurts most when you are alone or rooted, so don't stand still.
Poke Irelia with Spell Flux from range, then follow with Overload so it hits harder and bounces to any other marked enemies.
Mark Irelia with Spell Flux before Rune Prison so she is rooted, not just slowed. A root stops her from diving onto you.
Do not spend Rune Prison while Irelia is charging Defiant Dance. She takes less damage and the charge cannot be interrupted.
Stay away from minion waves when Irelia is near. She uses them to dash to you with Bladesurge, so keep your distance and keep poking.
Keep Rune Prison ready for when Irelia dashes in with Bladesurge. Rooting her right away cuts her trade short.
Step out of the line of Flawless Duet's blades. Being stunned in melee range is how Irelia kills you.
Spell Flux first, then Rune Prison, so Kassadin is rooted instead of slowed. Use the root to land Overload.
Kassadin takes less magic damage, and all of your damage is magic. Win lane through repeated trades with short-cooldown spells, not one big burst.
Hold Rune Prison for when Kassadin uses Riftwalk to dive on you. Rooting him in place leaves him exposed.
Kassadin's Null Sphere cancels channels. Open Realm Warp only when he can't reach you, since interrupting it cancels the portal.
Stay out of Force Pulse range when it is ready. It slows you and sets up his follow-up.
Push and harass early, before Kassadin reaches level 6 and Riftwalk lets him jump on you freely.
Cast Spell Flux first, then Rune Prison, so Katarina is rooted instead of slowed and cannot dash away from you.
Hold Rune Prison for when Katarina commits with Shunpo. If you root her, she is stuck in your range.
Stun-free Katarina is hard to stop, so keep Overload ready. Fire it down the lane when she lands on you, since it hits the first enemy in line.
Move away from Katarina's Daggers on the ground, since she gets a slash and faster Shunpo when she picks one up.
Do not stand near Katarina when Death Lotus is up. Move away from her once it starts, because she must stay near you to keep hitting.
Cast Spell Flux on LeBlanc first, then Rune Prison to root her and finish with Overload.
Rune Prison roots a Fluxed LeBlanc, so she cannot dash back with Distortion's return as easily. Use it when she dashes in.
Sidestep Ethereal Chains; it is a straight line that the first enemy hit blocks. Move away before it breaks, or you will be rooted.
Keep Spell Flux on LeBlanc's mirror image targets in mind: the clone is harmless, so hit the real one after she turns invisible.
Start trades with Spell Flux, then use Rune Prison so it roots Lissandra instead of only slowing her.
Hit Overload last, after Flux is on the target. It deals extra damage to Flux targets and refreshes off your other spells.
Stay out of Ring of Frost range while it is on cooldown. Walk up and trade when it is down, since her root is how she catches you.
Stand behind your minions so Ice Shard hits them first and you avoid the slow.
If Lissandra casts Glacial Path to dash in, use Rune Prison on her before she recasts. She cannot recast while rooted.
Back off when Lissandra reaches level 6. Frozen Tomb on you means being stunned and in range of her damage.
Walk up and cast Spell Flux first, then Rune Prison, so Lux is rooted instead of slowed and cannot step away.
Sidestep Light Binding; it stops at the first two enemies, so keep minions out of its path or stay out of line with them.
Spam Spell Flux when you are safe; its short cooldown keeps Lux marked and sets up a strong Overload.
Do not stand still in Lucent Singularity. Leave its area before it detonates so you are not slowed and hit.
Stay out of Lux's line when Final Spark is ready. Move sideways as soon as the red warning beam shows.
Walk up and hit Malzahar with Spell Flux first, then Rune Prison; he is rooted instead of slowed and cannot walk away.
Trade when Malzahar has just taken damage. His Void Shift cuts most of the damage he takes while it is up, so wait for it to drop before you commit.
Stay out of the line between the two portals of Call of the Void. Being silenced stops you casting your whole combo.
Overload hits Malzahar harder when he has Flux on him, so land Spell Flux first and then fire Overload.
Do not stand near minions carrying Malefic Visions. They can die and pass it to you.
Hold Rune Prison and Overload until Mel has used Rebuttal; it destroys projectiles, so Overload is wasted if you fire it into the nova.
Rune Prison targets the enemy directly, so use it to get Flux onto Mel and root her before she lines up Solar Snare.
Sidestep Solar Snare; it is a straight-line orb, and being rooted in Mel's field leaves you taking steady damage.
Back off when you are low once Mel has hit you a lot; her stored Overwhelm damage can execute you on the next hit.
Spread Flux with Spell Flux on Mel and her minions, then follow with Overload to hit everything marked.
Use Spell Flux freely for its short cooldown, then Rune Prison when Rebuttal is down to trade safely.
Put Spell Flux on Naafiri first, then Rune Prison, so she is rooted instead of slowed and cannot dash out of your range.
Fire Overload at Naafiri once she has Flux on her. It hits much harder and also bounces to her nearby packmates that have Flux.
Keep your distance and use Spell Flux often to poke her. A short cooldown lets you keep Flux on her every time she steps up.
Do not rely on Rune Prison as she dives. Hounds' Pursuit and The Call of the Pack make her untargetable, so hold your spells until she is targetable again.
Open with Spell Flux, then use Rune Prison so she is rooted instead of slowed. Follow with Overload for extra damage.
Look at where her Ball sits. Her damage only lands around it, so trade when it is far from you.
Stay out of her Command: Shockwave range around the Ball when you trade. Back off when she is level 6 and the Ball is near you.
Spend Overload's two runes by casting Spell Flux and Rune Prison first. You get the speed boost to walk out of her range.
Open with Spell Flux, then follow with Rune Prison so Qiyana is rooted instead of slowed. A rooted Qiyana can't dash away from you.
Fire Overload at Qiyana while she has Flux on her. It hits much harder and bounces to other Fluxed enemies.
Keep Spell Flux going on Qiyana from long range. Its short cooldown lets you poke her whenever she steps up for minions.
Stay out of Audacity range when it is ready. She dashes through you, so don't stand alone near walls or brush while she can reach you.
Hold Rune Prison for when Qiyana dashes in with Audacity. Rooting her mid-fight cuts off her escape and her follow-up.
Don't fight near river or walls once she has level 6. Supreme Display of Talent stuns you against terrain, so keep your fights in open lane.
Cast Spell Flux on Sylas first, then Rune Prison, so he is rooted instead of just slowed and can't lunge or run away.
Fire Overload at Sylas once Flux is on him; it hits much harder and spreads to other Flux targets.
Sylas heals when Kingslayer hits you, so trade hard while he is low and keep your distance when he is not.
Stay out of the line of Abscond / Abduct; if the chains hit, you are stunned and knocked up while he gets close.
Keep your Spell Flux and Rune Prison ready when Sylas dashes in. Rooting him as he arrives blunts his all-in.
Fight Syndra inside the range of Rune Prison and Spell Flux. Flux first, then Rune Prison roots her, so she can't dodge or run.
Keep the Flux on Syndra before you throw Overload. It hits much harder and bounces to other Flux targets.
Stay out of line with Scatter the Weak and don't stand next to her Dark Sphere. A pushed sphere stuns you.
Trade right after Syndra uses Scatter the Weak. Its cooldown is long, so she has little to stop you.
Overload has long range and a short cooldown. Use it to poke Syndra when you can't safely reach her with Flux.
Put Spell Flux on Taliyah before Rune Prison, so she is rooted instead of just slowed.
Cast Spell Flux on Taliyah first, then Overload; it hits harder and bounces to other Flux targets.
Stay out of Unraveled Earth stones when her Seismic Shove is ready; being shoved into them stuns you.
Sidestep Threaded Volley; it flies in a fixed direction, so move across its line.
Use Rune Prison to root her when she casts Seismic Shove, so she can't follow up cleanly.
Open with Spell Flux, then use Rune Prison so Talon is rooted instead of slowed. That keeps him in range for your follow-up.
Aim Overload at Talon while he has Flux on him. It hits much harder, and it still reaches him from long range.
Keep Spell Flux on the minion wave and on Talon so you can poke him. It has a short cooldown, so you can cast it often.
Hold Rune Prison for when Talon jumps in with Noxian Diplomacy. Rooting him there lets you hit him with your other spells.
Stay back once Talon has used Shadow Assault to disappear. Poke him again when he comes back into view.
Watch the lane before you use Realm Warp to join a fight. Talon roams a lot, so check where he is before you leave.
Start trades with Spell Flux, then follow with Rune Prison so the enemy is rooted instead of slowed.
Step away when Twisted Fate has the Gold Card ready; it stuns on his next attack.
Cast Overload on a Fluxed target for much more damage, and it bounces to other Fluxed enemies.
Stay out of a straight line with Twisted Fate; Wild Cards hits in a wide fan and hurts when you trade.
Watch for Destiny; it means Twisted Fate may teleport to you. Stay near your team or move away.
Cast Spell Flux first, then Rune Prison, so Veigar is rooted instead of slowed and cannot walk out of your follow-up.
Use Overload on Veigar when he has Flux on him; it hits much harder and also bounces to nearby enemies with Flux.
Keep moving sideways while Dark Matter falls, and walk out of its circle. Step in to trade only after he has used it.
Stay out of the edge of Event Horizon. Walking into the middle of the cage is safe, but touching its edge stuns you.
Veigar's Baleful Strike hits the first two enemies, so do not stand behind a minion in its path.
Avoid low health when Veigar reaches level 6, because Primordial Burst hurts more the lower you are.
Open with Spell Flux, then follow with Rune Prison so she is rooted instead of slowed and can't walk out of your combo.
Fire Overload at Vex after Flux is on her; it hits much harder and bounces to other Flux targets.
Don't dash or blink next to Vex without need. It marks you with Gloom, and her next hit does bonus damage.
Stay out of Personal Space range when her fear is ready. Her scream hits close around her, and the fear makes you flee.
Keep poking her with Spell Flux at long range; its short cooldown lets you trade often.
Sidestep Mistral Bolt early; it slows down its spread then speeds up, so wait until it narrows before moving.
Watch your health around level 6; Shadow Surge lets Vex dash onto you from afar, so don't stand low and alone.
Cast Spell Flux first, then Rune Prison, so Viktor is rooted instead of slowed and cannot walk out of your follow-up.
Overload hits much harder on a target with Flux, so mark Viktor with Spell Flux before you fire it.
Stay out of Gravity Field. If you are caught inside it, walk out before it stuns you.
Hextech Ray is slow and easy to sidestep, so move sideways when you see Viktor aim it.
Trade while Viktor's Siphon Power is on cooldown. Without its shield, he is easier to burst.
When Arcane Storm lands on you, keep moving, because it follows you. Fight out of it or run away rather than stand in it.
Spread Flux with Spell Flux first, then land Rune Prison to root Vladimir instead of just slowing him.
Do not cast Rune Prison into Vladimir's Sanguine Pool; he is untargetable in it and wastes your cooldown.
Stay out of Sanguine Pool's range when he sinks in, since enemies inside get slowed and damaged.
Hit Vladimir from long range with Overload; he has to walk up to use Transfusion on you.
Do not channel Realm Warp near Vladimir; a slow will not stop it, but a stun would cancel it.
Walk up and trade when Xerath is out of Shocking Orb; his range is long, but he is easy to reach and can't hit you while you stay close.
Use Spell Flux first, then Rune Prison, so Xerath is rooted instead of slowed and cannot walk away from your trade.
Cast Overload on Xerath after Spell Flux lands; it hits much harder and spreads to any Flux-marked minions or enemies nearby.
Sidestep while Xerath charges Arcanopulse; he is slowed and stuck casting, so a quick sideways move makes his beam miss.
Stay out of Shocking Orb's line, and keep a minion between you and Xerath when you can; the orb stops at the first enemy it hits.
When Xerath starts Rite of the Arcane, dive onto him or stun him if you can; his blasts are slow and he cannot easily dodge in close.
Keep Xin Zhao at range with Spell Flux and Overload. He wants to charge in and hit you three times, so make each approach costly.
Put Rune Prison on Xin Zhao as he charges in. If he is Fluxed it roots him; otherwise it slows him.
Move away when Xin Zhao's Three Talon Strike is running; his third attack knocks you up. Staying out of his reach stops the combo.
Respect Xin Zhao at level 6; Crescent Guard knocks you back and stuns you if you are not Challenged. Keep your distance when it is ready.
Flux the enemy first, then fire Overload for bonus damage while Xin Zhao is still approaching.
Use Rune Prison on Yasuo when he dashes in; once Spell Flux is on him, it roots him instead of slowing.
Poke with Spell Flux often; its cooldown is short, and Flux on a target makes Overload hit harder.
Stay away from Yasuo's minion line. He can dash through minions with Sweeping Blade to reach you, so keep your distance.
Hold Overload if Yasuo has just raised Wind Wall; it is a projectile and will be blocked.
Move sideways when Yasuo has two stacks of Steel Tempest. His next one is a whirlwind that knocks you up.
Put Spell Flux on Yone first, then use Rune Prison so he is rooted instead of slowed. Then follow with Overload.
Yone has no ranged answer in lane, so use Overload from long range and keep him from reaching you.
Aim Overload down a line with minions in it. It stops at the first enemy it hits, so it is easily wasted on a minion in front of Yone.
Rune Prison him when he starts Fate Sealed's windup? Better to stay spread from your team, because it pulls everyone it hits toward him.
Yone's Soul Unbound leaves his body behind, so when he is in spirit form, fight him then. He wants to hit you and snap back.
Cast Spell Flux first, then Rune Prison, so Zed is rooted instead of slowed. A rooted Zed can't dash out of your follow-up Overload.
Poke Zed with Spell Flux while he stands near his Shadow. It has a short cooldown and spreads Flux to everyone nearby.
Zed becomes untargetable while he dashes in with Death Mark. Save Rune Prison to root him once he lands, then back away.
Hit the enemy with Overload when it is marked with Flux. It deals much more damage and bounces to other Flux targets.
Use Overload's two charged runes for a burst of Move Speed when you need to escape after Zed's all-in.
Put Spell Flux on Zoe first, then use Rune Prison so she is rooted instead of slowed. Rooted is your best moment to hit her.
Stay out of the line of Sleepy Trouble Bubble. Sidestep it, because it stops at the first enemy it hits, so a minion in front of you can take it.
If Sleepy Trouble Bubble puts you to sleep, her next hit wakes you and deals bonus true damage, so keep your distance from her beforehand.
Hit Zoe with Overload while she stands at the end of Portal Jump. She cannot move there, so she is easy to hit.
Do not stand at long range in a straight line from Zoe. Paddle Star hurts more the further it flies, so step out of its path or stay close.
